edits_note: edits for the default scenario; other scenarios differ only in planting year / weather file named in their description

soil.note: available water = soil water minus LL15 (crop LL is unset in the founder's file); available water is capped at DUL (so the maximum is plant_available_water_mm); water above DUL is shown as water_above_dul_mm

limitations: INDICATIVE, NOT VALIDATED: the APSIM-X oil-palm model has not been calibrated or checked against any observation for this site or for Sumatra (the founder's model notes say BunchSizeMax was fitted to Papua New Guinea data and RUE follows Henson & Dolmat 2003).
Only the Mambang Muda point is supported: there is no APSIM run for any other location.

Palm age is an assumption, not the estate's: the founder's file plants on 2001-01-01, but run past about 2021 the model breaks (palms 25 years old: leaf area goes negative and APSIM aborts). The copy used here plants on 1 January of an assumed year (default 2012, so about 14.8 years old in Oct 2026) and starts the clock that day. Real block ages, density and management are unknown.

Soil provenance is undocumented: layer values look partly measured and partly template defaults; a single 2 m profile represents the whole point; initial water and nitrate in 2001 look implausible (spun up since).

Weather: history 2000-2022 is a nearby station series (about 8-9 km away, source undocumented); 2023 onward is an Open-Meteo model grid cell. The two sources differ (see weather_inputs.overlap_check), so the splice can shift the water balance. Forecast days use forecast rainfall, which is uncertain.
Free Open-Meteo tier is non-commercial; this is a demo.

The class on APSIM numbers is taken from APSIM's water-stress index (1 - fw) using the same provisional 0.3/0.5/0.7 cut-offs as the simple bucket (no citable source). It is a different quantity from the bucket's soil depletion: in the model fw = palm transpiration / demand, and transpiration is limited to a supply rate (sum over layers of KL x (soil water - LL15), about 3.5 mm/day in Aug 2026), so fw falls below 1 on high-demand days even when the soil is wetter than field capacity.
Not a yield forecast. The model reports FFB yield in its annual outputs but that is not served or claimed.

thresholds.applies_to: stress_index = 1 - fw (APSIM water-stress factor). Same provisional 0.3/0.5/0.7 cut-offs as the simple bucket, but a DIFFERENT quantity (APSIM supply/demand, not soil depletion): do not compare classes across the two sources

scenarios.description: Default. Palms planted 2012-01-01 (about 14.8 years old in Oct 2026, assumed), Open-Meteo weather as delivered.
Sensitivity: palms planted 2008-01-01 (about 18.8 years old), same weather.
Sensitivity: palms planted 2016-01-01 (about 10.8 years old), same weather.

Sensitivity: Open-Meteo rain from 2023 scaled by 0.74 so its 2013-2022 annual total matches the founder's station (planted 2012). Shows how much the result depends on the rain source; not a calibration.

evaluation.partial_year: year after the last full year, up to the last day of the weather file (includes forecast days); NOT a full year, do not annualise
evaluation.weather_note: 2023-2025 weather is a HINDCAST (Open-Meteo archive, grid cell near the site); it is not a forecast of future seasons. Annual FFB needs a full year, which is why a hindcast window is used.
evaluation.planting_year_note: ASSUMED (founder's 2001 planting breaks the model beyond ~25 y). Palm age in 2023-2025 is about 11-14 y under this assumption.

management_scenarios.fw_definition: fw = APSIM palm water-stress factor (EP/PEP), 1 = no stress

exist_and_varied_here.how: multiplier on every N rate in the founder's 'Palm Management' manager code, from 2023 (the founder's code sets rates by palm age; amounts are hard-coded there)
3 doses (15 Jan/May/Sep, founder) vs 6 equal doses (15 Jan/Mar/May/Jul/Sep/Nov)
the founder's file contains an Irrigation model but nothing applies water; we ADD a rule-based manager (trigger on fw, fixed mm, minimum days between)

do_not_exist: phosphorus and potassium fertiliser (the model simulates N only)
a dedicated leaching-prevention practice (cover crop, slow-release N, drainage control): leaching is only an OUTPUT; the only levers that influence it are the N rate and N splitting above
irrigation scheduling beyond the simple rule we add (no soil-moisture sensors, no forecast-driven rule)

units.ffb_t_ha_yr: t fresh fruit bunch per ha per calendar year: sum of the model's per-harvest 'HarvestFFB' ([Units("t/ha")], from the OilPalm model source) added up by the founder's manager as Calculations.Script.AnnualYield (report column 'Calculations.Script.AnnualYield' in AnnualOutput)
units.n_leached_no3_kg_ha: kg NO3-N per ha leached below the 2 m profile (sum of [Soil].SoilWater.LeachNO3: 'amount of N leaching as NO3-N from the deepest soil layer')
units.irrigation_mm: mm applied (sum of [Irrigation].IrrigationApplied); 1 mm over 1 ha = 10 m3
units.drainage_mm: mm drained below the profile (sum of [Soil].SoilWater.Drainage)
